messages.subject: SPDE and measurement error model
parts:
Hi:

I am gradually getting to know the INLA methods, and have been playing with various exercises/models (posted papers and a new book about R Inla).  I am currently reading  "Measurement error in GLMMs with INLA   by Muff, Rieble, etc..), and have been estimating those SPDE-related examples.  I was able to add some besag type spatial component too.  

But, I am interested to apply SPDE approach (using mesh) to this  measurement error model like the one on page 24 of that paper: 7.2 --Influence of systolic blood pressure on coronary heart disease.   It has three columns or 3 equations.)  

I was wondering if there is someone out there who has written any codes for this type of measurement error model(with covariates).  Thanks. 


Best,
Alok

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] SPDE and measurement error model
parts:
Hi Alok,

In the last chapter of the R-INLA book you can find the basis for that.
You have to add the covariate terms for the first (the covariate) part
of the linear predictor. Them you have to copy this linear predictor
part for the second one. You can find how to do it in the "Space-time
coregionalization model" example in the draft SPDE tutorial.

Elias

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: SPDE and measurement error model
parts:
I think you swapped n and n.spde towards the end? xi.field should be 1:spde$n.spde when constructing the stack, not u.field, which belongs to the iid model. For the iid model, either use
  A=1
  u.field=for each observation, index for which iid component to use.
or a use u.field=1:n, where n is the number of iid components, and construct a matrix A that extracts the needed component for each observation.  The former approach is easier, and the inla.stack function actually translates that internally into a model of the second type!

Finn

Thank you all for your kind tips. I really like the stack option and the spde in general. (Must admit that there is a steep learning curve, but a great many resource is available too.  Havard has been great in giving tips.)   I am working on a model, and I will have some questions (especially about how to use the weight with idx.x while doing the stacking --7.2 blood pressure example.  In the stack option, I created idx1.x idex2.x and idx3.x for each of the three stacks, and I also have three weights.).  I do not know if this will work;  I am running that model and do not know if it will be give some sensible results. 

Meanwhile,I have a question about the spatial field and how to use them in the model with 3 likelihoods. My experience has mostly been in using spatial lag in a single eq regression case.  My intuition says that the introduction of spatial field in each of the three likelihood (equations)  should be done by providing some sort of relative scale ?  Is this correct?  If so, is this what we are talking about?

y1 = ...   b1*sf
y2 =  .... b2*sf 
y3 =  ...  b3*sf

2.  Could we not have done just b3 = 1 and estimate the other two b1 and b2 as hyper parameters? 

3. Additionally, does it make any sense to do the following by introducing the three different spatial fields without any scale:

y1 = ...   sf1
y2 =  .... sf2 
y3 =  ...  sf3

Thanks.

> talking about?
>
> y1 = ...   b1*sf
> y2 =  .... b2*sf 
> y3 =  ...  b3*sf
>
> 1. Should I set b2 =1 = b3?  Then use the copy commands.  Is this the
> case of a shared spatial structure  structure for all data
> likelihoods?
> 2.  Could we not have done just b3 = 1 and estimate the other two b1
> and b2 as hyper parameters?

Hi,

yes, the easiest is to use the copy feature where you set b1=1, and
then estimate b2 and b3 (as copy where you use fixed=FALSE, as the
hyperparameter there is by default fixed to be 1).

> 3. Additionally, does it make any sense to do the following by
> introducing the three different spatial fields without any scale:
>
> y1 = ...   sf1
> y2 =  .... sf2 
> y3 =  ...  sf3

that is a modelling issue. you could also do something inbetween,
making them share the same hyperparameters, using the 'replicate'
functionality

Best 
H
